description: How a town's government is organized, as the record value News shows under the government's name: the term public sources use for its recorded form of government. Each move is a recorded form; data/english/government-form-moves.json files each recorded form under its move. Mostly from the U.S. Census Bureau's Individual State Descriptions for the 2017 Census of Governments, with a city's own page where the Census Bureau does not use the term.

mining.read: U.S. Census Bureau, Individual State Descriptions: 2017 Census of Governments (issued April 2019), its municipal sections for every state and its Appendix A; City of Dunedin, Florida, page on 100 years of its commission-manager government (March 3, 2026); Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government, news release on the 50th anniversary of its merged government (January 19, 2024).
mining.rule: Each part is the source's own term for the form, cut from its sentence and capitalized as the first words under a heading.

source.document: Individual State Descriptions: 2017 Census of Governments ("Most cities have an elected mayor-council form of government")
Individual State Descriptions: 2017 Census of Governments ("They are administered by a mayor-council, council, or council-manager form of government.")

Individual State Descriptions: 2017 Census of Governments ("operating under either the city manager plan, the mayor-council plan, or the commission plan of government")
Individual State Descriptions: 2017 Census of Governments ("Most towns have either an open town meeting or a representative town meeting form of government.")
